newsitem.title: FINLAND: MERITA RECOMMENDS NOT BUYING 2001, 2010 BONDS.
newsitem.headline: MERITA RECOMMENDS NOT BUYING 2001, 2010 BONDS.

text.p: Merita Bank said on Thursday it was not recommending clients to take part in auctions of the 2001 and 2010 Finnish government serial bonds on Thursday.
"Neither bond being auctioned is especially attractive -- instead, we favour the 2004 or 2006 benchmarks," Merita wrote in a pre-auction comment.
"I think the auctions will probably not be all that interesting to investors this time," Merita debt market analyst Juha Lehtonen said by telephone.
The previous auction in December of the 10-percent 2001 paper brought in 1.02 billion markka.
"Even though the 2001 is quite liquid, it is also quite expensive on the yield curve," Lehtonen said.
"(It) is relatively expensive and the spread to Germany is narrow," the bank said in the pre-auction note.
The 2010, which is not a benchmark, was unlikely to receive much interest, Lehtonen said adding that in previous auctions of 2010 paper only about 200-300 million markka had been sold.
"The 2010 bond is still illiquid ... but with a reasonable 45-50 bp premium over the 2006 it can be recommended on a buy and hold basis," Merita said.
The outcome of the state treasury's bond auctions is due to be published after 1330/1130 GMT.
